item.description:
## 一、隐藏的信号：硬件之战其实是"世界扫描"之战
David 关于 Muse Charm 的"热辣观点"值得深挖——但他只说对了一半。Zuckerberg 不是在收集数据来"绘制世界"，他是在收集**人类交互的第一人称语义流**。这与 Google Street View 的历史有惊人对称：Google 表面上做地图，实际上训练了整个计算机视觉时代的判别模型。Meta 正在做同样的事，但对象是"日常人际语境"。
**真正让人意外的观察**：这也解释了为什么 Muse Charm 定价刻意亲民、外形刻意可爱（那个"adorable yeti"）——它必须让人愿意在公共场合佩戴。可爱是隐私攻防的伪装术。回想 Google Glass 十年前失败的核心原因：那副眼镜"看起来像间谍设备"。Meta 学到了教训——用萌感换来的社会容忍度，比任何技术参数都珍贵。
## 二、被忽略的反常识：Agent 的"人格"不可防御，但"推定性"可以
对话中最锋利的一刀是这个区分：**personality is not defensible, but presumptuousness is**。这

item.title: [Business of Sport] From Near Fatal Car Crash to Winning the World Cup | Rishabh Pant
item.dc:creator: Business of Sport
item.content:encoded:
💡 创造性洞见

一、意外观察：那次车祸不是"打断了他的职业生涯"，而是"救了他的商业头脑"

大多数人会把 2022 年那场几乎致命的车祸讲成一个励志故事——"从病床到世界杯"。但如果仔细听 Pant 自己的叙述，会发现一个极其反直觉的事实：在车祸之前，他其实是一个"金融文盲式的天才"。

他自己承认："maybe for first five few years I didn't even know [what to do with the money]... I only got to know after co after my accident that I have to focus on all this aspect of the game also."

换句话说，IPL 给了他"疯狂的钱"，但是那场把他钉在床上 40 天、让他 629 天无法打国际比赛的车祸，才第一次逼他从"隧道视野"里抬起头，看见了资产、家庭、投资、基金会。他把身体的骨折转化成了认知结构的骨折——原本单核的大脑（cricket only）被迫长出了新的处理模块。

这里有一个残酷的悖论：如果没有车祸，他今天可能仍然是"更纯粹的球员"，但也更可能是那种 35 岁退役后被身边人骗光积蓄的印度体育富豪典型。这场事故实际上是他财富的守护者，而不是掠夺者。

二、跨领域连接：Pant 的"同心圆思维" ≈ 巴菲特的"能力圈" ≈ 佛教的"曼陀罗"

他在采访中不经意地画了一个模型："there is the core core circle for me... then there is a circle outside where I see all this money coming in..."

这个"同心圆"模型让我联想到三件事：

  1. 巴菲特的 Circle of Competence：核心是你真正懂的东西，外面是"来钱但你不控制"的东西——巴菲特一辈子在守核心圆，Pant 则是被迫从外圆倒推回核心。
  2. 禅宗曼陀罗：中心是本尊（板球 = 他的"本我"），外围是护法（家庭、财富、基金会）。他所说的 "I want to be the main guy in the mind instead of what they want me to create" 几乎是曼陀罗修行的世俗版。
  3. 产品经理的 Jobs-to-be-Done：核心工作（击球）不能被外围工作稀释，但外围工作反过来定义了核心工作的意义。

惊人的一点是：Pant 从没读过巴菲特，也没修过禅，但他在病床上"自然长出"了这个结构。这暗示了一个更深的系统性真相——当一个高强度专注者被强制中断专注时，他会本能地建构出"同心圆式"的注意力分配架构，因为这是有限认知资源在多目标下唯一可持续的拓扑结构。这不是他学来的，是被打断后的默认涌现。

三、隐藏系统性真相：印度板球正在制造"两代人之间的认知断层"，而 Pant 正好卡在裂缝上

采访里有一段被主持人快速带过、但极其重要的对话——Pant 说："as a kid I only wanted to earn like \$200,000... I'll do a little FD and the interest will come."（做个定期存款吃利息）

FD（Fixed Deposit）思维 vs. 股票/创投思维——这不是两种投资偏好，这是印度城镇化过程中两代人的世界观差距。

Pant 生于 Roorkee（北阿坎德邦的小镇），少年时的财富上限想象是"20 万美金 + 定存"。但 IPL 让他 19 岁就跨过了这个数字。这意味着他的内在货币操作系统（OS）和他的实际资产规模之间，出现了 100 倍量级的不匹配。

这里是被所有人忽略的系统性洞见：IPL 造就的不是"有钱的球员"，而是"心智还停留在小镇 FD 时代、但银行账户是新加坡家族办公室量级"的一整代人。这个错位如果不主动修复，就会以三种方式爆发： - 被身边人（他自己也承认过 "people scam you"）系统性收割 - 过早退役后陷入身份真空 - 或者反过来——用板球训练的极端纪律去"暴力破解"金融学习（Pant 正在走这条路："taking classes... 5–6 years"）

Dhoni 那句"你要一两年的成功，还是 15-20 年的职业生涯"，表面上是关于板球，深层上是在说：你能不能让你的心智 OS 跑赢你的银行 API。

Pant 是这一代印度球员里少数在车祸后被迫直面这个断层的人。他现在做的不只是"投资"，而是在给自己心里那个"20 万美金 + 定存"的小镇少年，做一次延迟了 10 年的操作系统升级。这才是他"我还没到达潜力"这句话背后真正的意思——不是击球平均分，是他整个自我系统的版本号还没跟上他的人生规模。

📝 转录文本

From Near Fatal Car Crash to Winning the World Cup | Rishabh Pant

开场：事故、心态与选择

主持人：You had a major life-threatening car crash in 2022. Is there a Rishabh Pant before and after that crash?

Pant：I think the accident taught me more about life. It was crazy time for me, man. Like seriously, I tried to make it very normal but from inside I know sometimes it takes away your soul.

As a kid I had only one thought — I want to play for India. It's a crazy competition, especially in India, and cricket is our number one sport. 1.4 to 4 billion people are there and you have to give whatever it takes.

IPL has changed the life of cricketers for sure. The kind of money — some crazy money. Playing cricket is one thing, but taking care of your family, being financially free — in that mindset it plays a huge part.

I haven't reached my potential. I want to be as authentic as I can because I don't like filters.

My wife — Mahendra Singh Dhoni — told me one thing: "You want to have success for one, two years, or you want to make your career for like 15, 20 years? It's up to you."

Business of Sport — fascinating.

一、欢迎与近况：落选 ODI 阵容

主持人：Rishabh Pant, welcome to Business of Sport in London. I'm pretty excited about it.

Pant：Me too, and thanks for having me here.

主持人：Thank you for coming in. Honestly, it is great. We love to do these in person. You come at an interesting time on the cricket side because the one day team was announced yesterday and you weren't selected for India. How has that sat within the cricketing mindset that you have at the moment?

Pant：Definitely, you know, you feel bad when something like this happens. But as an athlete's mindset — we always say that when there is a setback, there is always a comeback. As long as these are things you have to deal with day to day.

When people talk about "this happened to me, that happened to me", I think as an athlete this is part and parcel of the game. But at the same time, as an individual — how hard you're working, how clear you are in your path — sometimes it's not easy to maintain at this level.

If you're clear in your mind, and you have to see it in your mind first — a lot of people say that, but to make it happen every day, there is a voice in your head which is very constant. In a very disciplined manner you have to train it, over a period of time, that no matter what, you have to keep pushing, you have to keep getting better.

It's easier to make opinions all the time, but people have to wait for things to happen. A small thing — we were playing a Test match a few days ago and I got hit on the shoulder. It was really, really painful for me. It's been like 15–20 days. That moment happened in the game for 3–4 days, but for me my shoulder is still paining. People might see it for like five seconds, but the person going through it will go through it for at least the next 15–20 days.

主持人：Do the doctors want you to be resting?

Pant：Doctors always want you to rest. If you got to keep listening to the doctors, we are always sleeping and resting. So where we going to make things happen for us?

二、专注与纪律：板球作为一门"生意"

主持人：How important is focus for you within cricket? You're a player that has played different formats.

Pant：You have to have a holistic approach. It's very hard to pinpoint everything. When I'm playing cricket, it's easier for me to be very disciplined — it's like a business for me. I know how it runs: this is my mindset, this is the area I keep on working on. As an athlete you want to improve yourself each and every day.

Having that clarity in the mind takes time, because you have to leave a lot of things behind and still want to focus each and every day. Especially during setbacks, you feel like "I don't want to do this anymore." But there's the mindset, there's the discipline — you know that you're going to make it happen.

主持人：So this is your mindset — I'm going to get back in the team.

Pant：Yeah. There is no doubt that I have to make it happen, because I feel from inside that I haven't had the best opportunity to give my best. International cricket, all of sport, is changing all the time. Sometimes you have to wait for your chance and make things happen in a bigger way.

三、2022 年车祸：一次改变生命的经历

主持人：I have a feeling this is going to influence a lot of how you talk about various things in your life — you had a major life-threatening car crash in 2022. Is there a Rishabh Pant before and after that crash?

Pant：I would say yes, for sure. For me it was a life-changing experience. I wouldn't say it's a setback, because I like to see my life in a positive way. Words are those, situations will be those, but how you take those situations and make them work for you — that is up to you. There's one guy who is always having a conversation with you: your head. You have to be stronger than your head, because it's going to go everywhere.

The accident, like you said, taught me more about life. I'll be honest — I was not even thinking about life, this and that. When you are so much deep into something, you're not even thinking about what's happening around you. You are just trying to be the best version of you.

Before the accident, you have to be crazy about something to make it happen. It's a crazy competition, especially in India — 1.4 to 4 billion people, and cricket is our number one sport. You know you have to give whatever it takes. So you have to cut down your life and make it streamlined — you are only focusing on this.

That's why with people around me I always tell them: "I'm playing cricket. I'm giving whatever I have in my life for cricket, and everything else just revolves around it. There will be a time when I will not play cricket — then I can give everyone enough time. But till then I want to be focused, streamlined, because I want to give my best."

从"隧道视野"到"感恩视角"

主持人：So Rishabh beforehand was cricket — it was tunnel vision. And Rishabh afterwards is "I have multiple things that are important to me."

Pant：I agree. After the accident, one thing which has improved a lot is how I see life in a gratitude way. I have a broader perspective. Family is also important, work is also important — focusing on my cricket is still priority number one, but life has more to offer. You have to be nice to people regardless of how you're feeling, bad or good. You start appreciating life in a better way rather than just being inside the tunnel.

病床上的一个问题

主持人：Can you remember, after it happened, when was the first time you actually thought about cricket?

Pant：In my mind it was always like that. For the first 7 months, the kind of pain I had to endure was unbelievable. Especially for the first 3–4 months it was crazy, because with a knee injury you have to do rehab — everything is so stiff. I'm a wicketkeeper, so I have to squat. I need more range than anyone else in the cricket field.

Firstly, I never doubted that I'm not going to play cricket. It just didn't come to my mind — maybe here and there, because everyone was giving me that feeling that I might not be able to play in my life. Even the doctor was thinking that. But I never had a thought in my mind that I might not play. The only thought was: how quickly can I play?

When I was in the bed I asked the doctor one question — very heart to heart. My doctor's name was Dr. Dinshaw Pardiwala. He's the best in the business, for sure. The way my injury was — I broke almost every ligament in my knee.

I asked him, "Boss, man to man — what do you think? Tell me good or bad, it's okay, but you can tell me."

He told me: "Rishabh, I can guarantee you'll start living a normal life, but as of now it's looking a long road ahead."

I said, "Give me a time frame. Whatever time you give me, I'm going to do it before. Six months, whatever — I have to cut down the time."

This was when I was in the hospital — I was there for almost 40 days. So this conversation happened in the first 15 days. In my mind I was like, "I need to get back regardless of how people wrote me off. I know I can do it." Every day motivating myself through it was the biggest challenge.

629 天的康复

主持人：I hope this number is right — it took 629 days to return to international cricket.

Pant：When you're doing such a long rehab, you actually start forgetting like — why am I doing this? You start questioning yourself. Six months on the bed — imagine a person doing everything on his own, going around the world playing every day. I'm someone who doesn't want to sit in one place — I'm always out and about. Now I'm bedridden. I need help to even stand up for months. I started walking without crutches in 9 months.

It was crazy time for me, man. Seriously, I tried to make it very normal, but from inside sometimes it takes away your soul from inside every day.

主持人：But now you say you like to live life with a positive spin. It's strengthened you. If you can do that, you can pretty much do anything.

Pant：That was a turnaround for me. Coming back to the circuit — and God was kind enough — I played IPL, we played the T20 World Cup and we won the World Cup. Imagine — 6–8 months sitting there, had a crazy accident. In my mind I was telling our captain Rohit Sharma, "Brother, you have to get me back." I was not walking enough, but in my mind there was no doubt — I had to make it happen. And when you're clear you want to make it happen, whatever it takes, sooner or later it's appreciated.

四、IPL：一场变成节日的联赛

主持人：Tell us about the IPL. We're fascinated by it. Most interestingly, because I can't tell you how many times someone creates a new league or club and they'll say, "Oh, but the IPL did it, so we'll be able to." It's been an incredible story of innovation in sport — while also being a really good business.

Pant：IPL is IP property of BCCI. But the way they have structured it — it has changed the life of cricketers for sure. As a business, it's one thing, but once you start playing there, it's like a festival, man. The more people get involved in different ways, the bigger it gets. It started with a league, but now it has taken over — commercial, this, that. It's getting bigger and bigger every year.

The kind of money — some crazy money — it changes the life of people. Playing cricket is one thing, but taking care of your family, being financially free — that mindset plays a huge part. You're freer. For me it didn't matter — as a kid I always wanted to play cricket to the fullest, and that's a mindset I still take. Everything comes as a byproduct.

第二代 IPL 世代

主持人：You wouldn't have had the IPL growing up. So we're probably in the first generation of players fully playing — say born 2007.

Pant：I think second generation almost.

主持人：Now you have 15-year-olds doing amazing things.

Pant：It's been a great addition. For us it's a life-changing experience, but as a kid — when you get something so big, opportunities become massive. Otherwise the exposure was very limited. Now the exposure has gone to a different level, especially for a domestic circuit. It's still a domestic league, but such a big tournament — feels like a festival around the world. For us as Indians it has helped us grow our skill in a different way.

主持人：Do you look around now at some of the kids coming through and think "this talent is exceptional"?

Pant：Definitely. The way the game is getting bigger and bigger, this is icing on the cake. It's helping us develop our cricket to the root level. The competition is getting bigger, the pool of players is getting bigger, the exposure is getting bigger — you have to be on your toes and keep making it happen.

五、噪声、专注与 Kohli 的启示

主持人：We have a problem in this country — when a 16-year-old footballer scores one good goal, suddenly he'll be on the back pages, "Is he as good as Messi?" We jump so many steps. A huge part of being successful has to come down to your ability to appreciate the noise but focus internally.

Pant：When you are getting into the scene, you want to have that impact — as a kid, everyone likes you. Suddenly after 2–3 years… as an athlete the graph is always up and down. It just doesn't go like this — until you are Virat Kohli. He's been exceptional throughout his career.

主持人：Does he have an ability to focus that lets him not be affected by outside noise?

Pant：You don't have a choice. If you start focusing on what's happening outside, you tend to forget. Everything you do in your life will be questioned, will be challenged — good or bad. Every decision is challenged. The bigger you become, the pressure is going to mount. And he's someone who's been at the pinnacle — I've played with him for 8–9 years of international cricket.

When you go overseas, what it takes to win a match — that's a mindset. When someone is pushing that pedal so hard, leading from the front, you want your teammates to follow that route. It's not easy to win overseas. When you're playing in local conditions, you're so used to them — you've practiced so many times. But overseas you have to adjust to different conditions, thought process, tactical awareness. The perspective becomes bigger and bigger — and that's the challenge.

六、"品牌 Pant"：表演者、真实性、导师

主持人：Brand Pant — when I think of you from a cricket perspective, everyone who listens knows I'm a big cricket fan — you're a showman, an entertainer. Something happens when you play, particularly in a Test match environment. That's not necessarily the brand a lot of players have. How do you view how you approach the game?

Pant：One thing I've always felt — I haven't reached my potential. I'm getting there, improving day by day. For me it's always about giving my 200%, not even 100. I want to be as authentic as I can because I don't like filters. Be it on the ground, be it off the field — I like to be myself and trust whatever I'm doing. Everything I do in life can't be right, but it's not always about right or wrong. Sometimes you have to explore.

For me this is uncharted territory — never played international cricket as a kid. Growing through the years, you start learning, getting the exposure you never thought you'd get, and figuring out what's best for you. Nothing here is from a template — there's not someone in my home or family who has done this.

Yes, you can always have mentors — I have some of the world's best mentors, on the game and off. MS Dhoni is definitely one of them. Learning about the depth of the game.

I've always felt: learn from the best in the business. I have more chance of doing better if I learn from other people's experience — because I wanted to do everything very quickly. If I don't learn from others' experience, I can say "I know this," but from inside you don't. Having all the knowledge, then making a road plan for how you want to take it forward — that's the clarity you have in mind, and you make your move.

七、商业头脑的启蒙：父亲的一句话

主持人：You've been doing more and more work in business — investing, stock markets, early stage companies. Your foundation too. That kind of focus allows you to unlock all of this properly — fully committing.

Pant：As a kid I never thought about doing business. But as you keep growing, with time and exposure, you understand there is more to life.

My father always told me one thing: "When you start sitting with only your age group, you're not improving." He always wanted me to sit with people with more age, more experience, so I learn more.

I never understood as a kid — I said, "Why is my father telling me to stay with older people?" I only understood the meaning in the last 10 years. As a kid, whatever we hear from parents, we feel "Why are they saying this?" — but there's a lesson behind everything, most of the time. As kids we're on our ninth cloud, we feel we know everything. But in life it's not like that.

So opening up my thought process about businesses is a vertical which has opened for me, and it's very fascinating. When you open up that vertical, your mindset becomes bigger and bigger.

主持人：The reason people don't like it is because they hate feeling uncomfortable. What your dad said is really cool — it's forcing you to grow.

Pant：To be uncomfortable to learn something. But it's only uncomfortable if you take it as that. You take it as growth: "I don't know anything about it today, but I'm going to know a lot about it next week." Step by step. In one day you wouldn't know everything; in one day you will not forget everything. I'm still very young. The earlier you start, the better. I've seen a lot of athletes get into this mindset very late in their careers.

I still want to focus on my cricket 200%. But whenever there is time, I want to occupy myself with a good thought — that I'm building something, adding value. Everyone you meet is doing something good in life. It's about finding that balance — which I never had, because I was so focused. But it's part and parcel of the game.

主持人：It's not too late. You're still playing, still right at the top, and you just said you don't feel like you've reached your potential.

Pant：Because I have the advantage as a kid — I got to start playing the sport very early. In the last 8–9 years of playing at the top level, I've learned so much. I'm still 28–29. I still have so much to learn. I'm really excited over the next 5–7 years to unlock my full potential — cricket, business, lifestyle. I feel that energy from inside: it's going to be crazy the next 5–10 years for me.

八、四岁的第一支球棒，与十亿人的痴迷

主持人：Do you remember the first time you picked up a bat?

Pant：I do. Maybe four years old.

主持人：I've been to India, watched cricket in India. I came out for the 2023 World Cup with my wife. I was in the Wankhede, Mumbai, when you played Sri Lanka. And Ahmedabad — the 125,000-seater. That stadium… I've never heard a noise like it. Siraj and Shami steaming in — poor Sri Lankan batsmen, three for five. Driving around Mumbai afterwards, kids on grass playing — some without bats, just a branch off a tree. From the youngest of ages, this is something you absolutely obsess over.

Pant：Everyone starts with that thought — you love the game, anywhere you get time you start playing. At the top level, if you're not loving the game enough, then what's the point? If you get a chance to showcase your talent at the top stages of the world, you have to enjoy that moment.

That's why people say "focus on the process." The thought is simple: you are only thinking, "What can I do to give my 100%?" Yes, the result is in your mind — you want to win, perform better — but the ups and downs are so much you have to be very clear you're giving your 200%. Because nothing is guaranteed. You might practice for two months every day, no break, and still score a zero. Or you might not give your 100% and still score runs. Nothing is guaranteed, but you give yourself the best chance with commitment, discipline, focus.

九、金钱、圈层与被骗的风险

主持人：How much of a focus, if at all, has money been — financial security, optimizing the talent — you being the highest paid player in the IPL, doing big commercial deals?

Pant：There are two types of mindset. Why I started playing cricket was: I wanted to represent my country and I love the sport. That was my core goal.

You have a few circles inside your heart and brain. This is the core core circle for me. Then there is a circle outside where I see all this money coming in — but I don't know what to do with this.

For the first few years I didn't even know. I only got to know after the accident that I have to focus on this aspect of the game also. You start learning. You keep talking to the best people available. I've been fortunate to have the right set of people who guide me through ups and downs and keep me grounded. When you're talking with people with experience, you're not flying all the time — or if you're flying, you'll get to know, "Bro, this is not right." Surrounding myself with the right people helped me focus on day-to-day life.

Then you make circles: core circle — enjoy cricket, play to the fullest. Another circle — money coming in, invest it the right way. Because when you're focusing somewhere, people scam you also. It has happened. You're like, "Ah, this is my guy, that is my guy." Sometimes because you're focused in cricket, you lose focus here and there. Then you start thinking, "No, I need to focus a little bit on other areas."

主持人：One of the biggest dangers in sport nowadays is that young athletes can make a lot of money very early, and don't know how to manage it — get dragged into a world they weren't prepared for. For the profile of cricket in India, do you consciously feel like you have to say, "Right, feet on the ground, focus"?

Pant：This is a very conversation which I'm very constant with. I don't want to think that "Oh Rishabh, you are this or that." I just want to think: this is what's in my hand. I'll listen to the advice of the people around me, but have my own thought process — because I want people to build what I want to create, instead of what they want me to create.

Sometimes that can be a distraction — you get caught up trying to soak in from everywhere, but you're not you. I tell my team: "I want you to make my thought process bigger. I don't want it to be the other way around." There are so many people around you. Yes, you trust them, but you want your personality to be the main guy in the mind.

Sometimes what you're thinking might not be politically right. That's the hardest part. As a human being, sometimes you have to be politically right — the way you speak, the way you think, everything is under scanner. You can feel one thing at the bottom of your heart, but there are pros and cons of everything.

关于媒体："保持安静也是好的"

主持人：Even from a media perspective, it could be a real challenge to put the real you across.

Pant：One of my mentors taught me — I don't do too much media. Whatever respect there, there is okay, but I try to keep a very low profile. I do it when I have to, but most of the time I try not to expose myself. Sometimes you're thinking in the best interest of everyone, but the bigger perspective is not always right. You feel little shy that "I don't know how it's going to be put up." You might be thinking best, but if you're in a different mindset, you wouldn't take it in a positive way. It's very hard to find that balance. When I feel the balance is not there, I stay away.

He taught me: "Keeping quiet is also good." So I'm working on that. Because I want to feel free — but being free comes with a lot of cost. You can be free only at your home. Outside, everything matters — good, bad, your movement, everything is under scanner. You have to be clear what you want to do, move with precision, and enjoy whatever comes with it. Anything we are doing now is not the destination — it's a journey.

I made a quote: "International cricket is not a destination. It's a journey." As a kid I had only one thought — I want to play for India. Then I played for India when I was 19. Now what? Then I wanted to play all three formats, become the best, this, that. You have to keep ticking boxes. There is always a bigger goal.

As a human being you have to keep giving yourself bigger goals — beyond what you can even imagine. Life will make it happen for you. You can't think big enough. If as a kid you'd asked me, "What do you want to do now?" I would have said, "I have no idea. I wanted to make it crazy — but as a kid I only wanted to earn like \$200,000."

I'm from a very small town from Uttarakhand — a town called Roorkee. My mindset was: "I'll do a little FD (fixed deposit) and the interest will come." Because we didn't get enough exposure outside.

In Hindi we have a saying — when you're getting all the success, fame, everything, how difficult it is to digest it. That's the hardest part. My wife — Mahendra Singh Dhoni — told me one thing: "You want to have success for one, two years, or you want to make your career for 15, 20 years? It's up to you." That stuck with me. Since then I have never thought about the shortcoming — always work on the bigger goal, keep improving.

十、代表印度的重量：从达到目标到如何"消化"它

主持人：You said as a kid you just wanted to play for India — hundreds of millions of kids want that. The percentage chance of actually achieving it is tiny. When people finally get there, they often say either it's not as good as they thought, or they don't know how to deal with it.

Pant：That's the hardest part — sometimes you don't know how to deal with it. That's why having the right people around you when you're upgrading every 3 months, 6 months, 1 year — you need people who have seen it, who know how to digest it. You don't want a 3–4 year career, you want 15, 20 years representing your country. I feel proud to represent my country. I get goosebumps whenever there's a national anthem on the field — it takes me back to when we used to do school prayers. That "wow" feeling from inside, that gratitude: "Thank you, God, that I'm able to represent my country at the highest level."

十一、板球的三种形态：白球、红球、五天的浪漫

主持人：When you were seven, eight years old — was Test match cricket the thing?

Pant：For me it was always about only cricket. That time there was never a conversation about white-ball cricket and red-ball cricket. The conversation has started in the last four to five years more now. When things are growing, keeping them in check is harder.

As a cricketer you want to play cricket at the fullest. You don't want to think, "I can only play this or that." As a kid growing up, I would say I was too much ahead of the time — in my hometown Roorkee we used to play 10-over matches. Since I was a kid I've played so much white-ball cricket — what we call now. I'm so used to it. It's just getting that mindset and stability to express yourself.

In the last four years I haven't played much white-ball cricket. One is performance, one is I haven't got enough time to showcase my talent. I'll do whatever it takes to make it happen. Let's not make our opinion based on any narratives — people start their career when they're 26–28. I'm lucky I've played 8–9 years of international cricket. That experience only helps, and the ladder only moves up.

对不同形态未来的看法

主持人：Are countries outside England, Australia and India strong enough to play Test cricket? Longevity, attendances, what's the best. Over the last five years there's been more conversation about cricket in general than ever before.

Pant：If you're not careful, we're going to lose certain parts of the game — when things are expanding, it's always hard to keep everything in check. Good will come, some bad will come. But there's a good signal that cricket is a growing sport around the world.

You can't always think about longevity or all these things — you got to take one thing at a time, give your best, keep moving forward. Longevity isn't about "how can I get my career longer" — you want to play cricket, especially at international level. You want to be the part of the crowd, or you want to be the one making the difference. It takes a lot from inside to make that happen every day. Pain, mindset, setback all come back in a circle — a round circle which keeps on happening in sports life. Anyone with long careers has to go through it.

主持人：Do you think that passion for Test match cricket is there just as much as it has been?

Pant：Two places I can promise you it's still there — England and Australia. Appreciation of the longer format at the highest. In the longer format everything is tested — discipline, focus, motivation, zeal. So much up and down in a single game. It tests your character, your mind. That's why we call it the purest form of the game. Especially with the WTC (World Test Championship) coming in and matches getting results, interest has actually come back to Test cricket. The format which is suffering the most, I would say, is ODI. T20 and Test cricket are still doing fairly well.

主持人：I love the 50-over format. It captures an experience in a day. We love experiences. T20 is 3.5–4 hours. But I still want that day. I want five days — I'll happily go and watch. But there's a cost if 50-over cricket goes.

Pant：Sometimes you leave that balance to the officials who are doing that job. As an athlete, you want to be inside the game, playing it to the best.

十二、印度球迷、海外巡回与美国的新市场

主持人：You like playing here, right? The communities of Indian fans in this country — I've been in stadiums here where I'm like, "God, this could be a home Test."

Pant：We have been fortunate as an Indian cricket team — wherever we go, our fans are there through thick and thin, good or bad. Always supporting us everywhere in the world.

主持人：Did you play in America? What was that like?

Pant：Amazing atmosphere. We played three matches of the World Cup in New York. Anywhere we go, it's such a big community — stadiums were full. Playing cricket in the US is a different exposure. They made a new stadium from nothing, just for the World Cup. Things are moving in the right direction — the game is growing, the exposure is growing. People are getting interested in different markets. And it's not only India — people support all the teams. Even England — this country loves cricket. When you perform here, you can feel that respect even on the ground. Overseas they'll put you to the hardest test, but once you've earned it, these people show lots of love and respect too.

十三、基金会与回馈

主持人：Tell us about your foundation.

Pant：It's been an interesting project for me personally. As a kid, I always wanted to give something back to the society. I've been doing it for years — I just wanted to put some structure to it, in a bigger way. On a personal level you can't make it big enough. If I can impact anyone's life in a better way, why not? Especially for my hometown — the state Uttarakhand — I feel there's so much in my heart I want to give back, and I'll start from there.

主持人：What's the main work?

Pant：Right now I haven't gone specific — someone in hospital I help them, maybe education I help them. As of now it's been very random. But I want to put a structure so I can scale it up and help more people. Doing it, I feel good from inside — especially after the accident. I have that satisfaction. When you're doing something like this, have no expectations from other people. Just keep doing the right thing regardless.

团队合作与协作

主持人：Are you guys — the big squad of players — a close-knit group? Do you collaborate on ventures?

Pant：As of now it hasn't been the best of ecosystems to have collabs. But things are changing in a big way. People want to indulge with each other in a better way — especially with something like a foundation which can help a lot of people. If there are a lot of crossovers helping each other, that's a really interesting concept.

十四、legacy：不刻意，但方向正确

主持人：Is legacy something you think about?

Pant：It's very hard to define how you want to do things every day just because you want to create a legacy. Life doesn't work out the way you want always. But if you're doing the right stuff step by step — doing business, being focused in cricket, looking after your family — small steps in the right direction. Legacy is in the back of the head, but you can't emphasize it every day. It has to run in the back of the mind, but you start doing the smaller things in the right way. Move in that direction, and legacy will follow.

十五、投资、股市与"学习"的复利

主持人：How patient are you with yourself when doing this work away from the pitch?

Pant：It was hard in the starting. This is a new skill I wanted to add. When you're only focused in one direction, your mind is not opening enough. I started learning about investing — I'm the one in the family who has to do everything on my own. I have to learn my finance, keep my head level. My mother — she has given me that freedom: "We trust you that you're going to do the right thing." That's the kind of family — standing behind you as a rock, no matter good, bad or sad. That's the kind of freedom you get. You get more confident as an individual.

主持人：On stock markets — we've done a lot of chat with athletes about startup investing, but not much about stock market side.

Pant：For me both aspects are very important. Stock market is easier — there is so much study which goes into investing in companies. I've been studying for 5–6 years, taking classes, learning how to invest. If you're putting your hard-earned money somewhere, you have to feel it from inside.

主持人：Taking classes?

Pant：Yeah, it's my hobby to learn.

主持人：In your free time, right? Because with sport, people often go, "Oh, as athletes you're busy all the time." But a lot of the time you're sitting in a hotel room.

Pant：Absolutely right. Whenever there is free time, I try to make use of it in a better way. I like to be in a mindset where I'm learning, improving each and every day.

I also want to look at few areas — maybe adventure sport, especially in India, in my hometown Uttarakhand. It's a big adventure sport destination. The idea is at an early stage but really looking forward. Especially with my business point of view and foundation point of view — I want to start all of these things from where I started my life, my birthplace, Uttarakhand. We call it UK.

主持人：You go to UK — it's Uttarakhand!

Pant：Yeah. So it's one area where I want to keep excelling.

从"消费者"到"创造者"

主持人：What about building businesses yourself?

Pant：Working on that. I want to keep adding stuff in my life rather than minusing something. Everything requires your focus. There were times I wasn't ready. Now, having balance in life, this also adds a lot of value. Really want to give some time to opening up businesses — discussing how an idea can become a real business, getting the work done. Opening up myself to different ventures, start investing, start creating — rather than just being a consumer all the time.

主持人：Has there been a movement in India for athlete-driven or creator-driven consumer products?

Pant：It has started in a lot of places, but hasn't taken off to the next level. That's where I come in. Why not?

主持人：What would you create?

Pant：I still want to be rich, so I don't want to create just one thing. Adventure sport is definitely one. Giving back to society. Focusing on cricket at the fullest. Multiple fronts.

主持人：Political answer, I love that! Well done.

Pant：Sometimes you have to.

十六、家人、旅行与"日本"梦

主持人：Being able to give back to those close to you — the sacrifices your mother made when you were growing up.

Pant：I've told my mother: "You don't have to think anything, you just do whatever you feel is right. I want you to be happy." We are always on the road working — you want someone to enjoy this and be happy. I feel so good taking care of my mother.

Even my sister got married last year. It was my father's dream — the way he wanted. Only 70–80 people. In India, when you do that kind of wedding, it's so hard — we have big fat weddings, like crazy. We wanted just friends and family, very close people. We missed a lot of close people because I was playing outside — we were playing Champions Trophy, and my sister was getting married 2–3 days after that.

主持人：Do you mind the travel element?

Pant：You get to learn so much when you travel. We can discuss everything in the world, but once you travel you meet different kinds of people. You understand how they see life, the exposure, the food, the culture. One of my favorite hobbies.

主持人：Favorite international food?

Pant：Japanese. It's my go-to food, man.

主持人：Have you been to Japan?

Pant：The one place I haven't been is Japan. My sister says, "You have to go, you have to go." I said, "Yes, at some point." Top of my list.

主持人：Me neither. But now I've started having kids… I want to go for two, two and a half weeks — like what my wife and I did when we came to India for nearly three weeks. You had the cricket, but you saw lots of different aspects of India and culture. Japan seems exactly like that — travel around, try different things.

Pant：That's what I've heard. Hopefully in future.

印度自身也变了

主持人：What country surprised you most from a cricketing perspective?

Pant：As a kid, everywhere I traveled surprised me. Because I've been all my life in India, and when I go outside — 10–15 years back India was also different. In the last 15 years the way India has grown as a country. I used to come from my hometown to Delhi because there was no cricket team there. I had to travel by local bus — it used to take 5.5–6 hours. Now the travel time has almost become half. There are six-lane, seven-lane, eight-lane highways.

Every place you go you learn so much — different food, different people. That's why sometimes I feel playing overseas leagues is really interesting — not only for money, but you spend a lot of time, understand how people play overseas, learn their culture, they're playing different kind of cricket. Insight of the game becomes better.

主持人：I will never forget when I first went to India — the noise. The roads, the horns. In England if someone uses their horn, they're being mean. In the taxi I was like, "What's he doing?" He said, "No no, we're speaking to each other."

Pant：It's like giving a signal that "I'm coming this way."

主持人：It was an attack on the senses, but in the best way. And look — the best thing about sport is that we went there and experienced that because of cricket.

Pant：One country I remember is New Zealand — so close to nature. Some places fascinate you. People are so nice — overly nice. Sometimes if someone is overly nice you feel, "Ah, he has some work." But then you meet them — they're genuine, very nice.

主持人：Incredible sporting culture. Four, four and a half million people. The strength of that cricket team over the last 30 years —

Pant：Every ICC tournament they still do good. I don't know the reason. Maybe pressure is less, expectation. People feel more free. That's something we need to add more to our textbook — playing with more freedom.

十七、IPL 的更衣室与"18 码 150 公里"的秘密

主持人：Is IPL an element which has elevated the game — where you all come together from different countries in these teams, get to know each other, build relationships?

Pant：It definitely changes the game. You're playing together, sharing the dressing room with the best in the world. You practice together.

I'll tell you a story — when I was a kid, playing for Delhi, 2016–17. Our fast bowlers were Shami, Pat Cummins, Kagiso Rabada, Kuldeep… I was 18. These guys were bowling crazy. I was facing them in the nets — and luckily I was smashing them. It gives you a different kind of confidence. "If I can hit the best bowlers in the world in the net…" There was a practice match — I did well there. Anywhere you spend time, you're hitting them — it gives you confidence that "I belong here, I can make it happen."

Sharing the dressing room, you learn. Till a few years into your career — absorb as much as you can from everywhere. Yes, it can be hard because everyone is doing their own thing, but if you can absorb, the thought process is going to help you like crazy.

主持人：Who are you most happy to have on your team, not playing against you?

Pant：Pat Cummins, Rabada, Shami… very hard to name one. They're good, man.

主持人：Who's the quickest you've faced?

Pant：From inside, I try not to feel who is bowling quickest.

主持人：It's just cricket.

Pant：Yeah. Mostly I practice at 18 yards, or maybe 16 yards — but I'm still batting at 150 kph. So you get more time in the game. When you practice at 18 yards at 150, when you're batting at 22 yards at 150, you're still batting 150 — but you get more time. So I practice in a way where everything becomes easier.

The hardest and fastest are, you know, sidearm guys — because I'm batting from 18 yards. We have Ragu — he's been with the Indian team 10–15 years, since Rahul, Sachin Tendulkar. This guy keeps us on our toes. We were practicing in Sri Lanka — he bowled me 12–13 bouncers in 15 balls. I said, "I want to practice a few other balls also."

But when you're used to so much pace in the nets, it translates. One ball I still remember — Mitchell Starc bowled me in Perth. I didn't even flinch. He just bowled and I did this — it went past, past my ribs, one-bounce boundary. Ball flying from here, one-bounce boundary — it flew like anything. Nipped back in. I was like, "Whoa, I'm going to die." In real time, facing 140+ kph, there's almost only 1 second, maybe less.

十八、"In the Zone"：空球场的静默

主持人：Have you ever seen the Roger Federer speech at a university? He asked, "Of my 20-year career, what percentage of points do you think I won?" Ultimately he said: "It's my ability in the biggest moments to capitalize, and to forget about what's gone." Are you good at that?

Pant：Absolutely. Once the ball is gone, it's gone. You have to be in the present. The next ball is coming — you have to be in the same frame of mind, playing at your best, not thinking about what happened. Maybe someone dropped a catch. Maybe he bowled an amazing ball. You can't stay in the past. Every moment in the game, you have to be in the present.

I remember one point — when the whole stadium is sitting, when you're in your zone, you can't hear anything. When you're focusing, you're just in the moment. You see the ball coming. You feel it's just the bowler and you. You can't hear any noise. It feels like an empty stadium because you're in your zone. There's time between deliveries, the field getting back — so you switch on and switch off. Once you're switched on — we call it a zone — you're not hearing anything. It's just you and the bowler.

主持人：Having sat in that stadium and listened to that noise — that you could block all of that out is amazing. And that was in a 35,000 stadium, not 125,000.

Pant：It is insane. These feelings can't be put into words. "Amazing" is the word. But you still can't think about that all the time — you still have to play the game at the fullest.

结语

主持人：There'll be plenty of time for you to reflect on your career in the future. It's amazing to hear you say you haven't reached your full potential yet. There's so much you could look at — the crash, disappointments, all the work outside the game — where you could go, "Okay, is this now all about cricket?" But to still ground it and want to push on is amazing.

We never get this insight into top-level athletics, particularly from that Indian cricket perspective. To hear the experiences firsthand is incredible. I'm so grateful. You said you didn't do a lot of media — I promise everyone he's not handcuffed to the table. It's been a lot of fun.

Pant：I hope so, man. Thank you for having me. Really appreciate it, brother. It's been great.

观看原视频 →

## 一、意外观察：那次车祸不是"打断了他的职业生涯"，而是"救了他的商业头脑"
大多数人会把 2022 年那场几乎致命的车祸讲成一个励志故事——"从病床到世界杯"。但如果仔细听 Pant 自己的叙述，会发现一个极其反直觉的事实：**在车祸之前，他其实是一个"金融文盲式的天才"**。
他自己承认："maybe for first five few years I didn't even know [what to do with the money]... I only got to know after co after my accident that I have to focus on all this aspect of the game also."
换句话说，IPL 给了他"疯狂的钱"，但**是那场把他钉在床上 40 天、让他 629 天无法打国际比赛的车祸，才第一次逼他从"隧道视野"里抬起头**，看见了资产、家庭、投资、基金会。他把身体的骨折转化成了认知结构的骨折——原本单核的大脑（cricket only）被迫长出了新的处理模块。

item.title: [Bits + Bips] Yields Are Up. So Are Bitcoin ETF Inflows. Why?
item.dc:creator: Bits + Bips
item.content:encoded:
💡 创造性洞见

一、被忽视的"反转"：当债务足够大，加息反而变成"放水"

Ram 抛出的观察极具颠覆性——当美国 30 万亿美元国债的期限结构短到快速滚动时，加息 25bp 反而向美国家庭"喷"出更多现金流。这是主流货币政策思维的镜像反转：央行以为自己在"抽水"，实际上在向持有短债的家庭部门发利息补贴。

这与传统"加息紧缩"叙事完全相反，却精准解释了本集最大的谜题——为什么美债 10 年收益率冲破 5.2%，比特币 ETF 反而录得 2025 年 10 月以来最大单周流入 24 亿美元？ 答案可能是：市场已经嗅到财政主导（fiscal dominance）的味道——利率越高，联邦利息支出越大，越接近"财政抑制 + 通胀货币化"的旧剧本。1940s、1970s 的历史正在第三次重演，只是这一次比特币成了 40 年代所没有的"逃生舱"。

跨领域连接：这个"债务规模翻转政策效力"的现象，其结构与生物学中的"剂量-反应曲线反转"（hormesis）惊人相似——小剂量的毒素抑制机体，大剂量却激活防御机制。宏观政策一旦越过某个"债务门槛剂量"，就进入了完全不同的相空间。

二、隐藏主线：整集节目其实在讲同一个东西——"边界正在崩塌"

表面上这集在跳跃：BitGet 被黑、Thor Chain 中立性、收益率、Oracle 信用、Meta Muse、Alpha School……但如果你把它们按"边界属性"重排，会发现一个共同的元主题：所有过去清晰的边界都在同时液化。

崩塌的边界 具体表现
去中心化 vs 中心化 Thor Chain 证明"能停机却不停机" = 主动选择做洗钱管道
加息 vs 宽松 短债滚动下加息 = 变相财政注水
Agent vs 人 但法律责任只能落在两条腿的人类身上
大学 vs YC Alexander Wang 从 MIT 辍学 → Meta 花数十亿买 Scale AI → 市值 +$5000 亿
公链 vs 私链 每一次黑客事件都在替 BIS 论证私有链的合理性

最刺穿的一句话来自 Austin："如果你的去中心化系统的主要结果，是让人们的钱被中心化的坏人偷走——那你根本没实现你想实现的东西。" 这不只是对加密行业的审判，而是对所有"用技术绕过治理"的意识形态的审判。

三、意外洞察：Zcash 复刻 2016 Bitcoin 的真正原因，是"AI 让隐私变成刚需"

Ram 说 Zcash 让他 déjà vu 到 2016 年的比特币——同样的人（Winklevoss 兄弟）、同样的价格轨迹（$600→$1000→$1500 两周内）、同样的社群温度。但他给的解释停在"隐私很有用"。真正被漏掉的因果链是——AI Agent 时代的到来，让"透明账本"从功能变成了漏洞。

想想 BlackRock 预测的 2027 年 10 亿个 AI Agent、每天 2170 亿笔交易——如果这些 agent 全用透明链，你的私人 concierge、私人医生、私人财富管理都会立即被广告商、保险公司、税务机关反向拆解。Илья 在节目里已经承认："我在 Ethereum 上维护 100 个地址的电子表格，就是为了防关联攻击。" 这不是极客洁癖，这是未来所有 AI 主导金融行为的必然瓶颈。

跨领域连接：这与生物学中"细胞膜选择性通透"的进化压力完全同构——单细胞生物一旦复杂化，就必须演化出选择性屏障，否则无法维持内部秩序。加密世界正在经历同样的"膜进化"：从裸奔的原核生物阶段（透明链），进入需要 Zcash/Miden 这类选择性膜的真核阶段。谁掌握"膜蛋白"（隐私协议），谁就控制未来 AI 经济的信号选择权。

四、被所有人忽略的最深一层：这集节目本身就是"AI 时代记者行业的墓志铭"

Bits + Bips 反复推销自己的"unchainedcrypto.com/survey"、newsletter、独立频道——这本身就是媒体在 AI 冲击下的求生动作。当 Muse 可以在 200 毫秒内做出比 LLM chatbot 更精准的分类决策，"人类记者手工筛选新闻"的商业模式正在被 Alexander Wang 那个 VM+LLM+外部 guardrail 的架构慢慢吞噬。

讽刺的是：节目里嘲笑 OpenAI"用恐惧营销"的三个人，自己正在用"订阅我们独立频道否则你会错过重要信息"做同样的事——恐惧稀缺性依然是内容分发的核心动力，只是包装成了"cleareyed, no shilling"的反 hype 姿态。这是本集最未被言说的元讽刺。

📝 转录文本

Yields Are Up. So Are Bitcoin ETF Inflows. Why?

Bits + Bips 节目转录

一、AI Agent 与消费级 AI 浪潮

Starts doing it. We're moving at the speed of willpower more and more every day. So, I think this AI agents is a extraordinary development. It's why I think semiconductors are a great opportunity.

Uh and Meta is first out there, but yeah, Google is coming. Google Spark is in testing right now. It's going to be compelling. Apple sees this. Everyone was going after the personal assistant AI. It was the obvious thing. But there are other AI coming: the personal concierge, the personal doctor, the personal wealth manager, what we're building at Lumida. All of these niches are going to get filled out.

So I think it's super exciting if you're long the AI trade, and we're going to be mainlining AI now to consumers. Right now it's been mostly infrastructure and compute story — this data center pol very abstract concepts. Now consumers are sourcing tangible value, like when they first got their AOL CD and went on the internet, right? That's what's happening now with these personal assistant agents.

二、财政抑制的历史循环与"加息即放水"的反直觉

Historically governments have always picked inflation if they can, right? We've done that in the United States repeatedly. If you look at the history of the 40s and 50s postwar — financial repression. If you were to go and then look at the 70s — financial repression. Every time we get into that position, we end up in that way.

And I think with debt-to-GDP where it is, there's a sort of counterintuitive thing that starts happening: if you have $30 trillion of debt outstanding — I will remind everybody 1% of the debt is $300 billion — if you raise rates 25 basis points, that's a lot more free cash flow in the hands of Americans, given that our debt is relatively short-term and rolling quickly.

Like there is some bizarro inversion of thinking that happens when the debt gets big enough where rate cuts are no longer restrictive, but in fact just spray more cash out as well.

三、BlackRock 预测：10 亿 Agent × 2170 亿笔日交易

They say the rise of agentic AI and machine-to-machine payments will likely increase demand for blockchains and other programmable payment infrastructure — stable coins, native crypto assets, etc. Existing rails such as card networks blah blah blah make them less suited to always-on, very low value transactions requiring programmatic execution.

So what did BlackRock basically say? They said there's going to be a billion agents in 2027. They said the billion agents are going to be doing 217 billion transactions a day, and those transactions are going to be settled on blockchain rails because traditional existing rails just aren't relevant for those kind of transactions.

And then you say okay, what's going to capture that value? Layer ones, hedging mechanisms, dexes because they're going to be trading in and out of different tokens. And then you start thinking to yourself, hold on a second, maybe this chart is actually conservative. Maybe the altcoins actually outperform Bitcoin by 50x.

Why? Because whenever you use a protocol, ask yourself a question: could an AI — and will an AI — actually use this protocol? Solana? Yeah, AI could use Solana. Hyperliquid? Yeah, AI could use Hyperliquid. Near Intents? Yeah, AI could use Near Intents.

四、加密的"多巴胺驱动社交交易"新范式

Now, how much more so when the validation is not only likes but actual money? And that's what crypto's created. It's created transparent trading machines where everyone can see P&Ls and people are starting to share it.

So, if you look at apps like FOMO, Pump Fun, we've created a master use case in crypto which is dopamine-driven social trading. And what I think is actually going to happen — if you take that and you combine it with a tokenization of everything — all of a sudden, you've got this industry which is a combination of a casino and a social network. But instead of casino, let's call it an investment house. An investment house with a social network — that's a monster business. That's more powerful than any social network.

And in fact, I kind of think that Elon Musk and Twitter have seen this because they're starting to incorporate trading into your Twitter. People are testing the Twitter buttons. So the ultimate social network doesn't only reward you with likes, but actually rewards you with increase in net worth.

五、Zcash：2016 年比特币的 déjà vu

六、做市商的"洗盘效率"寓言

If you were to set up a system that was designed to generate a lot of volume in the most efficient way — the funny part about this: who are the people who would generate half a billion dollars in volume off 3 million in open interest? People who are hyper-efficient.

Who are hyper-efficient? Market makers. That's their job — be as efficient as possible in what they do. So if you got two market makers and put them in a room and said, "Hey guys, I'll pay you $1 every time you cross each other." Those guys are going to rip your face off. They're going to create so much volume you wouldn't believe it.

Now the question is: does that have any benefit to an end user? Because that's the difference between wash trading — even if it's one person, two parties colluding together — and incentivized liquidity.

七、Muse：一种"分类器"式 AI 的降维打击

It's not an LLM that talks to you. A lot of information goes in, and then a classifier makes decisions for you, and those decisions come out with weights, and the thing is way cheaper and way faster — like 200 milliseconds fast.

So instead of you letting Fable drive your browser, and every pass is like "I'm going to take a screenshot of this whole thing, and I'm going to find the thing I'm going to click," and then it gives you like three paragraphs back about what it's finding — this thing is like "I'm going to look at everything, and I'm going to make a decision based on weights, and I'm going to choose the thing within 200 milliseconds." So it's a classifier, and it's making decisions very fast, and it's very cheap.

On my podcast, we kind of talk about the tension between effective and efficient. And you always do it effective first, and then you find a way to do it more efficient once you're doing it effectively.

I think we're going to see lots of different types of new kinds of models like Jev, where it's doing nearly the same task. As long as it's not a chatbot you're chatting with — it doesn't do the chatbot thing — but it can do a lot of these tasks and CI type things and browser-use type things way faster and way cheaper than just letting Fable click around.
